text: I’ll interpret each tread as a rectangular 1.100 m exposed radial run by 0.250 m tangential depth. Its solid extends inward to the axis and is unioned with the column, so the exposed inner end is exactly at the 0.100 m column radius and is supported without a zero-area tangent contact. Tread top elevations are 0.150–3.000 m; thus the twentieth tread is flush with the top plane. The air volume is the 1.200 m-radius shaft minus the column and tread solids. I’ll first build and render this coarse CAD volume before selecting/exporting patches.
The preview cell had a typographical syntax error and executed nothing. I’ll rerun the same single construction step with the render call corrected.

The CAD boolean and STL were created, but the installed PyVista plotting API rejected a rendering keyword; because the cell errored, it cannot be part of the reproducible script. I’ll repeat the construction and use Matplotlib’s headless 3D renderer instead.

The coarse view shows one connected air volume with the spiral obstructions and central column. I’ll now inspect the actual B-rep face types and centers so patch selection is tied to analytic surfaces (cylinders and known construction planes), not bounding-box position.

Inspection found a construction error: build123d cylinders default to being centered in Z, so the shaft currently spans −1.5 to +1.5 m and only the first ten treads intersect it. I’ll correct both cylinders to use a minimum-Z alignment, then regenerate the coarse view and verify all twenty tread levels appear on the fluid boundary.
The constructor supports explicit three-axis alignment. I’ll now rebuild only the affected solids and downstream fluid, using `(CENTER, CENTER, MIN)` in Z, and render the corrected air volume.

The corrected boundary contains all requested tread underside/top levels from 0.110/0.150 m through 2.960/3.000 m. I’ll select the two cylindrical faces by their analytic radii/areas, select floor and opening by their authored planes and outward normals, assign every remaining planar face to `treads`, and export all five patches together so shared STL seams use one tessellation.

The exported union is closed and consistently wound. For the coarse mesh I’ll use a 0.10 m Cartesian background grid, retain the connected region containing `(0.8, 0, 0.05)`, refine all boundaries to 0.05 m and the column/treads to 0.025 m so the 0.040 m tread thickness is represented. I’ll write the OpenFOAM meshing dictionaries, then run only `blockMesh` as the next coarse-stage check.
The background mesh is correct at 21,632 cells with uniform 0.10 m spacing. I’ll now run `snappyHexMesh -overwrite` to carve and locally refine the interior air region.
This OpenFOAM build requires placeholder `fvSchemes` and `fvSolution` dictionaries even for meshing; no geometry operation ran. I’ll add the standard empty dictionaries and rerun snappy.
The placeholders must contain the expected scheme subdictionaries in this version. I’ll supply minimal valid meshing-only contents and rerun.
Snappy completed successfully with 107,171 cells and retained all five named surface patches. I’ll run the binding bare `checkMesh` now and inspect patch counts and mesh quality.

The binding check passes: one connected 107,171-cell region, five patches, maximum non-orthogonality 51.2°, skewness 2.97, and positive cell volumes. I’ll produce a cutaway mesh image to visually confirm the spiral gaps and column are represented, rather than relying only on surface and quality statistics.

The mesh converted successfully and each named patch appears as a distinct VTK boundary dataset. I’ll render a vertical `y=0` slice of the volume mesh, which directly shows the shaft envelope, central-column exclusion, and tread-separated air passages.

The final slice confirms a full-height column void, twenty staggered tread intersections, and refined cells across each 40 mm tread. CAD volume is 13.2504 m³ versus mesh volume 13.2445 m³ (0.045% lower from snapping/tessellation). I’ll declare the completed geometry and mesh with no expected advisory exceptions.

The coverage advisory reports the intended complete partition: all 7,198 triangles are assigned exactly once across the five requested patches. I’ll waive that warning because it confirms, rather than contradicts, the requested patch coverage.
